9	# Queue Skill — Redis story_jobs Lifecycle
10	
11	Ordering matters: **enqueue → worker → monitor**. Fill the queue first, start worker(s) to
12	drain it, then check status. All three scripts target the framework's own Redis instance —
13	`127.0.0.1:${FINOPS_REDIS_PORT:-6380}`, db `${FINOPS_REDIS_DB:-1}` — **never** the
14	`finops-redis` instance on 6379 that story agents' own Flask/Celery apps use (those call
15	`flushdb()`/`flushall()` while testing; see `mental-model.md`/`AGENTS.md`'s Redis isolation
16	note). Never point any of these scripts at 6379.
17	
18	## 1. `enqueue.py` — fill the queue
19	
20	Manual `sys.argv` parse, confirmed `scripts/enqueue.py:143-152`:
21	
22	```
23	--dry-run        in sys.argv — print the plan only, don't write to Redis
24	--clear          in sys.argv — reset the queue (destructive)
25	--missing-only   in sys.argv — skip cells that already have a saved result
26	--interleave     in sys.argv — round-robin fill across models/providers so concurrent
27	                  workers spread across providers instead of hammering one
28	--model VALUE    read via sys.argv.index("--model") + 1
29	                  default: $FINOPS_MODEL, else "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
30	```
31	
32	```bash
33	python3 scripts/enqueue.py                                    # fill queue, default model
34	python3 scripts/enqueue.py --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5   # target a specific model
35	python3 scripts/enqueue.py --missing-only                      # skip cells with a saved result
36	python3 scripts/enqueue.py --interleave                        # round-robin across providers
37	python3 scripts/enqueue.py --dry-run                           # print the plan only
38	python3 scripts/enqueue.py --clear                             # reset the queue (destructive)
39	```

41	**Safety convention: never run `--clear` without checking queue state first.** The
42	opencode `enqueue.ts` tool's own gate refuses a bare `clear` and tells the caller to pass
43	`dry_run=true` alongside it "to see what would be removed" — but tracing `scripts/enqueue.py`'s
44	`main()` shows this doesn't actually work: the `if dry_run:` branch returns *before* the
45	script ever reaches `if clear:`, so `--dry-run --clear` together just prints the normal
46	"Would enqueue N cells" plan, not a preview of what `--clear` would delete. There is no
47	flag that previews a clear. The real safety practice: check current queue contents with
48	`python scripts/monitor.py` (or `--json`) *before* running `--clear` bare — `--clear` takes
49	effect immediately and irreversibly once run without `--dry-run`.

51	## 2. `worker.py` — drain the queue
52	
53	Zero CLI flags — confirmed no `add_argument`/`sys.argv` parsing in the file; `main()` just
54	loops on Redis `BRPOP`. Env vars, `scripts/worker.py:22-24`:

58	FINOPS_REDIS_PORT   default: 6380
59	FINOPS_REDIS_DB     default: 1
60	```

62	Lifecycle is process management, not script flags:
63	
64	```bash
65	python3 scripts/worker.py &      # start (background); auto-exits after 2 min idle
66	pgrep -f "scripts/worker.py"     # status — list running worker PIDs
67	pkill -f "scripts/worker.py"     # stop all workers
68	```

70	Run N workers in parallel for N-way concurrency (`AGENTS.md`'s Commands block: "worker.py
71	— BRPOP worker — run N in parallel") — start multiple `python3 scripts/worker.py &`
72	processes.

74	## 3. `monitor.py` — check status
75	
76	Manual `sys.argv` parse, confirmed `scripts/monitor.py:114-116`:
77	
78	```
79	--watch    in sys.argv — live 5s-refresh loop, needs an interactive terminal
80	--clear    in sys.argv — deletes story_jobs/story_status/story_results (destructive)
81	--json     in sys.argv — machine-readable output
82	```

86	python3 scripts/monitor.py --json      # machine-readable — the canonical dashboard example
87	python3 scripts/monitor.py --watch     # live loop — run manually in an interactive terminal
88	python3 scripts/monitor.py --clear     # deletes queue state — destructive, run manually
89	```

91	`--json` is the canonical machine-readable dashboard invocation — this is the exact command
92	to run for "show me the queue dashboard" or any programmatic status check; there is no
93	separate dashboard script, just `monitor.py --json`.

96	needs a real interactive terminal — tell the user to run it manually) and don't run
97	`--clear` automatically (it's destructive — tell the user to run

102	- Redis isolation: this queue is `finops-queue` on port 6380. `finops-redis` on 6379

107	  that's expected once the queue drains, not a crash.
108	- `--watch` needs a real terminal — don't attempt to run it from a non-interactive agent

18	  `review_worker.py` pair manually.

20	  files into aggregates.

22	## `review_all.py` — synchronous, all-in-one
23	
24	Confirmed `scripts/review_all.py:119-122`:
25	
26	```

28	--story STR      default: "" — substring filter on story name
29	--dry-run        flag
30	```

34	python3 scripts/review_all.py --workers 3 --story task_manager --dry-run
35	```
36	
37	## `review_stories.py` — synchronous batch, no Redis
38

40	
41	```

43	```

55	(`scripts/trigger_reviews.py:60-77`):
56	1. Polls `analysis_jobs`/`analysis_status` Redis keys until drained.
57	2. Runs `enqueue_reviews.py` as a **blocking** subprocess (waits for it to finish filling
58	   `review_jobs`).
59	3. Then spawns `REVIEW_WORKERS` **detached** `review_worker.py` processes via `nohup ... &`
60	   — these keep running after `trigger_reviews.py` itself returns.

103	enqueue_reviews.py → (review_worker.py workers drain review_jobs) → finalize_reviews.py
